title: The length of an append is the sum of the two lengths
statement: For lists of naturals, the length of the concatenation of l1 and l2 equals the sum of their individual lengths.

formal.statement: theorem List.length_append : ((x0 : Sort (1)) -> ((x1 : List.{0} x0) -> ((x2 : List.{0} x0) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (List.length x0 (List.append x0 x1 x2)) (AxNat.add (List.length x0 x1) (List.length x0 x2)))))

evidence.supports: List.length_append is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example list_theorem_inventory -- List.length_append 2>/dev/null | grep -Fc '((x0 : Sort (1)) -> ((x1 : List.{0} x0) -> ((x2 : List.{0} x0) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (List.length x0 (List.append x0 x1 x2)) (AxNat.add (List.length x0 x1) (List.length x0 x2)))))')" -ge 1

notes: Needs Nat.zero_add (nil case) and Nat.succ_add (cons case) since this prelude's Nat.add recurses on its RIGHT argument, so `0 + x` and `succ a + x` do not reduce for symbolic x by defeq alone. Declared in the List/Nat bridge, after build_nat_prelude, for exactly this reason.
